findings.where: First screen and the whole tile: hero, texture panel and article specimen, at desktop and phone
findings.fault: Nowhere on the page shows Mark himself. There is no portrait, and no slot or stand-in shows where his photograph would go or how this stone and red look would hold it. The only picture area is the ashlar texture. The visitor sees a mark and a name set in capitals, but no face.
findings.who_objects: The bank official, who is choosing one named person to advise on a PPP law and wants to see who they would be writing to. Mark, too: the brief's client value 3 ('the man himself… Mark is seen') applies to every tile, and first-visit trust item 1 always applies to a solo practice.

findings.where: Hero, at desktop and phone: the large name 'MARK · M · MOSELEY / INFRASTRUCTURE · ADVISOR' in red Roman capitals under the dark arches, on a flat mid-grey ground
findings.fault: A name in tracked capitals, carved into grey under an arch and parted by interpuncts, reads at first glance like a memorial plaque or a foundation stone. It looks formal and monumental, not approachable. The ground is flat grey with no stone in it (the ashlar only appears inside the texture box), so the page also looks dim and greyed out, not like dressed stone.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose brand sheet (§5) asks for a personal, approachable advisor, not a reserved institution. The visitor's first impression is of something solemn or dated rather than a working advisor they can write to today.

findings.where: Every heading in minium red (hero name, article title, 'LAID · WEIGHTY · SETTLED', the 'CINZEL' specimen, the texture's capital M) against the 'WRITE TO MARK' button in the same red
findings.fault: The action colour is also the heading colour. When you squint, the huge red name outweighs the small red button, and red stops meaning 'act here'. The direction's own card says the one accent 'flows to the action', and the palette notes call minium 'the one action', but here it goes to every heading first.
findings.who_objects: A visitor scanning for how to get in touch: the button does not stand out from the text around it as the one thing to do. Under the house carriers table, the primary action's colour is reserved for it.

findings.where: Type pair rule ('always in capitals… words parted by interpuncts') as used in the hero h1 and the article specimen title 'THE WORLD'S BEST PUBLIC-PRIVATE PARTNERSHIP LAW'
findings.fault: The rule is applied in one place and not the other. The hero parts every word with an interpunct, which makes the middle initial 'M' read as a word of its own. The article title has no interpuncts at all. Even a short title runs to three lines of red capitals. Mark's real titles, such as 'Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the 'Abundance' Challenge', would run to four or five lines and be slow to read.
findings.who_objects: Angélique, who adds posts and has to follow a rule the specimen itself breaks (brief value 9). Also the reader of a long article title set entirely in tracked capitals.

findings.where: Hero 'WRITE TO MARK' button (mailto) and the page's end, which has no footer
findings.fault: The only way to make contact is a mailto button that hides the address. Nowhere on the page is the email address written out, and there is no footer to carry it. A visitor with no default mail program set up gets nothing when they click, and cannot copy the address.
findings.who_objects: An official at a development bank on a managed work machine, who often writes from webmail or forwards the address to a procurement colleague. First-visit trust item 7 asks for the address in full as its own link text on every page.

findings.fault: The line says what Mark advises on and gives one credential, but not where: no countries or regions of his work.
findings.who_objects: A bank official who hires against terms of reference that weigh experience in their region. They cannot tell from the first screen whether he has worked in their part of the world (first-visit trust item 6, and 'what a visitor must be sure of' for an advisor).

findings.where: Nav bar lockup 'MMM INFRA' and the hero mark
findings.fault: The logo has been recoloured. The wordmark is set in the near-black text colour instead of the logo blue #0070C0, and the arches are drawn in the page's 'cut' #2A2925 instead of the logo grey #404040. This was done without Mark's yes.
findings.who_objects: Mark: his brand sheet says the logo colours are open on #8 but not yet ruled, and the house rule is never to recolour a logo without the client's yes. Returning visitors who know the blue wordmark from his current site and documents also lose what they recognise.

findings.where: Hero 'WRITE TO MARK' button, the tabula ansata
findings.fault: The two dovetail handles are drawn as separate triangles with a gap from the panel. At button size they read as two arrows pointing in at the label, or as a bow tie or sweet wrapper, rather than as one inscribed tablet.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who does not know the Roman tablet. To them the button looks novel or playful, which jars with a senior legal advisor.

findings.where: Article specimen pull quote ('Whichever PPP Law I am currently working on…') against the hero button
findings.fault: The static quote takes the button's signature tabula ansata shape. One look now means both 'press this' and 'read this'. The parts map also flags the quote's own box as possibly looking actable.
findings.who_objects: A reader on an article page, where the same dovetailed shape will also mark the contact button. The house function walk (question 5) asks that each look mean one function.

findings.where: Palette swatches: GRANITE, MINIUM and LIME
findings.fault: The 'LIME' swatch is a red block with white tracked capitals 'AA', the button's own treatment, though it is static. Next to it, 'MINIUM' is a second red block, so a palette described as 'three colours' shows two identical reds. The 'GRANITE' swatch is an empty outlined box the colour of the page, which reads as an empty field.
findings.who_objects: Mark, reading the tile to rule on the palette. He cannot see what 'lime' looks like as a colour, and one swatch looks like a button.

findings.fault: Internal ticket numbers and repository paths appear in client-facing copy. They are set in the browser's default monospace, a third typeface that renders larger than the body text around it and breaks the stated type pair.
findings.who_objects: Mark, who reads the tile as his own site's look and meets meaningless internal references in an off-pair font.

findings.where: Article specimen byline 'MMM INFRA BLOG NO. 8 · 18 SEPTEMBER 2024'
findings.fault: The byline credits the firm's blog, not Mark, though the article is written in his first person.
findings.who_objects: Mark: brand sheet §5 says the individual is the brand, not a firm's voice. A reader arriving on the article from a social post also cannot see who wrote it.

findings.where: Article specimen, the related lecture row at desktop
findings.fault: The lecture title sits at the far left and its 'Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF' at the far right of a wide column, with a large gap between them. The date and format read as detached from the title they describe (proximity).
findings.who_objects: A reader scanning Mark's talks for the newest one, who has to track across the gap to tie the date to its title.
